fields.statement: At be216e8c (leaf commits d898ca6d and be216e8c): rhiza workflow check plan and plan-milestone are valid. workflow describe for both shows pr-green on.fail -> pr-green-infra -> pr-green-infra-wait -> pr-green, and the same loop for rebased-green. The infra wait steps use rhiza ship check --settled --changed --rerun-infra with a 6h timeout, a 30s interval and max_visits 3. go test -trimpath ./internal/workflow/... passes, including TestPlanBuiltin and TestPlanRerunsCIFlakes, which assert this routing. go test -trimpath -count=1 ./cmd/rhiza -run 'TestScripts/plan-workflow-ci' passes all four scripts. plan-workflow-ci-infra-wait runs the built-in plan workflow with a fake gh. wait-pr spends both --reruns 2 (run rerun 42 --failed appears twice in gh.log). The run view log has no failing test. pr-green fails into pr-green-infra, which passes into pr-green-infra-wait. The wait passes once the fake's new job is green, and pr-green passes on visit 2. The run then goes through rebase, rebased-green, merge (pr merge appears once in gh.log) and close-out, and succeeds. plan-workflow-ci-infra-timeout ends the run on a pr-green-infra-wait timeout, and run status names an infra failure. plan-workflow-ci-flake-red's log now has a FAIL line, so a red with a failing test still ends the run. The diff fixes attempt 1's finding f1. One limit: under the fixed test clock the wait's own backoff rerun is never due, so the green comes from the fake's new job, not from a rerun the wait issued.
